title: Tiered batching parameter sweep results (v1) — concurrency x prompt-length buckets
content:
Notes / how to read this sheet
- Purpose: early parameter sweep to compare proposed batching tiers (fast / standard / cost_efficient) across (a) concurrency and (b) prompt-length buckets, using a single representative chat route config.
- This is NOT a final pricing doc. “$/1M tokens” is a relative unit-economics estimate derived from measured GPU-time per request and metered token counts. Use deltas between tiers; absolute values will move with kernel/runtime changes.
- Workload: chat-completions, non-tool calls, temperature=0.2, max_new_tokens=256, stop=[]
- Each cell is p95 end-to-end latency (ms) and estimated $/1M total tokens (prompt+output). p95 is over 5-minute steady-state windows after warmup.
- Tokenization: OpenAI-compatible tokenizer for the model; prompt length buckets are measured in input tokens.
- Streaming: these runs are NON-streaming unless explicitly marked. (Streaming cadence checks tracked separately; fast tier queue-delay needs special handling.)

Assumptions / runtime knobs (sweep baseline)
- Model family: “RW-Chat-13B” (internal alias; similar prefill/decode profile to popular 13B chat models)
- Runtime build: runtime-1.21.0-rc2 + tier mapping behind flag (see redwood/pr_18435)
- Quantization: none (fp16 weights)
- GPU SKUs tested: A100 80GB (SXM), H100 80GB (SXM)
- Replica config: 1 GPU per replica, 1 replica (to isolate batching effects)

Tier definitions used for this sweep (v0 mapping)
FAST
- max_batch_tokens_prefill: 2048
- max_batch_tokens_decode: 1024
- max_queue_delay_ms: 1.5
- prefill_weight: 1.0
- decode_weight: 2.5
- admission: conservative (earlier shed)

STANDARD
- max_batch_tokens_prefill: 4096
- max_batch_tokens_decode: 2048
- max_queue_delay_ms: 4
- prefill_weight: 1.0
- decode_weight: 1.5
- admission: default

COST_EFFICIENT
- max_batch_tokens_prefill: 8192
- max_batch_tokens_decode: 4096
- max_queue_delay_ms: 10
- prefill_weight: 1.2
- decode_weight: 1.0
- admission: more aggressive batching before shed (but still respects global overload protection)

Legend
- Latency = p95 end-to-end request latency in milliseconds
- Cost = estimated $/1M tokens (prompt + output)
- Buckets: S=0–256, M=256–1024, L=1024–4096, XL=4096–8192 input tokens
- Concurrency = in-flight requests to a single replica (client-side concurrency)

TAB A — A100 80GB (SXM) results (non-streaming)

A1) Concurrency = 1
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 182 / 1.62 | 196 / 1.55 | 240 / 1.44 |
| M (256–1k) | 268 / 1.74 | 289 / 1.66 | 350 / 1.54 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 690 / 2.10 | 720 / 2.02 | 810 / 1.88 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 1530 / 2.82 | 1548 / 2.74 | 1655 / 2.55 |

A2) Concurrency = 4
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 205 / 1.55 | 232 / 1.43 | 300 / 1.28 |
| M (256–1k) | 315 / 1.67 | 372 / 1.52 | 470 / 1.35 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 770 / 2.02 | 840 / 1.86 | 990 / 1.62 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 1640 / 2.70 | 1745 / 2.52 | 2030 / 2.20 |

A3) Concurrency = 16
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 290 / 1.50 | 355 / 1.30 | 520 / 1.10 |
| M (256–1k) | 430 / 1.60 | 560 / 1.36 | 840 / 1.14 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 1040 / 1.92 | 1280 / 1.60 | 1750 / 1.28 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 2240 / 2.55 | 2750 / 2.08 | 3850 / 1.65 |

A4) Concurrency = 64 (overload edge; shedding starts depending on tier)
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 620 / 1.62 | 980 / 1.28 | 1700 / 1.05 |
| M (256–1k) | 980 / 1.70 | 1550 / 1.34 | 2700 / 1.08 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 2100 / 2.05 | 3400 / 1.58 | 6100 / 1.20 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 4300 / 2.65 | 7000 / 2.05 | 13000 / 1.55 |
Notes (conc=64):
- COST_EFFICIENT shows best $/1M but p95 becomes very sensitive to queue delay and KV pressure; some runs hit soft-shed thresholds (increased 429/503 in separate error-rate sheet).
- FAST keeps p95 lower but pays in $/1M due to smaller batches and more frequent kernel launches.

TAB B — H100 80GB (SXM) results (non-streaming)

B1) Concurrency = 1
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 132 / 1.18 | 140 / 1.14 | 162 / 1.06 |
| M (256–1k) | 205 / 1.26 | 220 / 1.20 | 260 / 1.11 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 540 / 1.54 | 560 / 1.48 | 625 / 1.36 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 1200 / 2.05 | 1210 / 1.98 | 1305 / 1.80 |

B2) Concurrency = 16
| Prompt bucket | FAST (p95 ms / $/1M tok) | STANDARD (p95 / $/1M) | COST_EFFICIENT (p95 / $/1M) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S (0–256)  | 210 / 1.10 | 255 / 0.98 | 380 / 0.84 |
| M (256–1k) | 315 / 1.18 | 410 / 1.02 | 610 / 0.86 |
| L (1k–4k)  | 780 / 1.42 | 980 / 1.20 | 1400 / 0.96 |
| XL (4k–8k) | 1680 / 1.96 | 2100 / 1.62 | 3100 / 1.28 |

TAB C — Summary deltas (quick view)
(All deltas are COST_EFFICIENT vs STANDARD unless noted)

C1) Unit economics improvements are strongest at moderate/high concurrency and short/medium prompts
- A100, conc=16, bucket S: cost -15% (1.10 vs 1.30), latency +46% (520 vs 355)
- A100, conc=16, bucket M: cost -16% (1.14 vs 1.36), latency +50% (840 vs 560)
- H100, conc=16, bucket S: cost -14% (0.84 vs 0.98), latency +49% (380 vs 255)

C2) For long-context prompts, batching helps cost but prefill dominates latency
- A100, conc=16, bucket XL: cost -21% (1.65 vs 2.08), latency +40% (3850 vs 2750)
- H100, conc=16, bucket XL: cost -21% (1.28 vs 1.62), latency +48% (3100 vs 2100)

C3) FAST vs STANDARD behavior
- FAST consistently reduces p95 vs STANDARD (especially at higher concurrency) but costs ~+8–18% $/1M tokens depending on bucket.
- At low concurrency (1–4), FAST’s latency wins are modest; STANDARD is often “good enough” and cheaper.

TAB D — Queue delay + batch formation stats (A100 only, representative)
(For debugging; pulled from runtime metrics added in redwood/pr_18449. Values are approximate p50/p95.)

D1) conc=16, bucket M (256–1k)
| Tier | queue_delay_ms p50 | queue_delay_ms p95 | formed_batch_size p50 (req) | formed_batch_size p95 (req) | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FAST | 0.4 | 1.6 | 2 | 5 | tight queue delay; batches rarely exceed 6 |
| STANDARD | 1.2 | 3.9 | 4 | 10 | stable; good util; fewer tail spikes |
| COST_EFFICIENT | 3.8 | 10.4 | 8 | 18 | highest util; p95 is very sensitive to burstiness |

D2) conc=64, bucket S (0–256)
| Tier | queue_delay_ms p95 | formed_batch_size p95 (req) | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| FAST | 2.2 | 10 | admission kicks in earlier; lower tail but less throughput |
| STANDARD | 6.1 | 20 | higher variance; some queue delay spikes |
| COST_EFFICIENT | 13.8 | 32 | most efficient but tail grows quickly; needs stricter overload hooks |

Open issues / action items from this v1 sweep
1) COST_EFFICIENT max_queue_delay_ms=10 is too high for some bursty traffic patterns (p95 explodes at conc=64). Proposal: cap to 7ms for non-streaming and 3ms for streaming (separate mapping) + rely more on max_batch_tokens to drive efficiency.
2) FAST tier decode prioritization: these runs are non-streaming; we still need to validate token cadence. Current expectation is FAST requires decode_weight >= 2.5 (see later streaming regression fix in redwood/pr_18463).
3) KV cache pressure: XL bucket at high conc pushes cost-efficient into higher KV churn; we should add a tier-specific KV pressure limit override (Omar has a WIP branch; aligns with later ENG-18424).
4) Next sweep should be per-model-family (7B vs 13B vs long-context) and include quantized variants; numbers here should not be used to generalize beyond similar prefill/decode ratios.

Appendix: Run IDs / reproducibility
- benchmark-lab template: benchmark-lab/pr_311
- harness config: bench_run_config=v1_tier_sweep_a100_h100_chat_256out
- seeds: 3 seeds per cell; report uses pooled p95 over merged traces
- raw logs: gs://redwood-benchmark-lab/runs/2025-02-19-tier-sweep-v1/ (internal)

Owner notes (Grace)
- These look directionally correct: STANDARD is the sane default; COST_EFFICIENT buys 10–25% $/1M at the expense of 30–70% p95 depending on conc; FAST trims p95 but pays ~10–15%.
- I’m still uncomfortable with cost-efficient at conc>=64 without tighter overload/backpressure coupling. Recommend we gate cost-efficient behind cohort opt-in + strict rollback triggers (p95 + error rate + queue delay).
